context.analysis:
## Overview
A cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and the US. The system guarantees regional data residency, regulatory compliance, and resilience for unstable internet connections.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) and Licensed Clinicians
- Pharmacies and National Pharmacy Networks (EU) / US Pharmacy Systems
- EU Telehealth Platform (GCP `europe-west3`) and US Telehealth Platform (GCP `us-central1`)
- AI Symptom Checker Engine with immutable audit logging sidecars
- Regional Identity Providers (EU eIDAS-compliant / US OAuth via OIDC)
- Regional Health Authorities and Auditors
- Managed Cloud KMS with Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK)

## Relationships
- Patients and Clinicians interact with regional telehealth platforms via HTTPS/REST and WebRTC for video.
- Regional platforms connect to National Pharmacy Networks and US Pharmacy Systems using national standards and HL7 FHIR over HTTPS/REST.
- Regional platforms call the AI Symptom Checker Engine via gRPC with strict local caching.
- Third-Party Identity Providers integrate via OpenID Connect (OIDC) over HTTPS.
- Health Authorities access regional audit endpoints via mTLS and signed JWTs over HTTPS.

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Deployed in `europe-west3` and `us-central1` for geographic isolation.
- WebRTC: Powers video consultations with adaptive bitrate streaming for connections below 300 kbit/s.
- HL7 FHIR & REST/HTTPS: Ensures US interoperability and secure API communications.
- gRPC: Facilitates low-latency internal communication with the AI Symptom Checker.
- OpenID Connect (OIDC): Manages regional identity federation.
- Cloud KMS (CMEK): Provides cryptographic data isolation per region.

## Rationale
The architecture strictly enforces data residency boundaries to comply with GDPR and HIPAA mandates. Regional isolation combined with localized AI processing and cryptographic controls ensures regulatory compliance while maintaining high availability for low-bandwidth users.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency while ensuring high availability and regulatory compliance.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU/US) using Flutter Patient Mobile/Web App
- Licensed Clinicians using React/Node.js Clinician Portal
- GCP API Gateway (Cloud Endpoints/Envoy)
- Core Telehealth Service (Go/Spring Boot)
- AI Inference Wrapper (Python/FastAPI)
- Consent & Profile Management Service
- Pharmacy Integration Gateway (Camel/Spring Integration)
- GCP GKE Regional Clusters (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`)
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL Databases
- GCP Cloud Pub/Sub

## Relationships
- Patients/Clinicians to API Gateway via HTTPS, WebRTC, and OAuth2/JWT
- API Gateway to Core Telehealth Service via gRPC
- Core Telehealth Service to AI Inference Wrapper via gRPC
- Core Telehealth Service to Pharmacy Integration Gateway via GCP Pub/Sub
- Services to Cloud SQL PostgreSQL via TLS

## Technology Stack
- Flutter: Client-side development supporting local caching for low-bandwidth degradation
- React/Node.js: Clinician portal web application framework
- Go / Spring Boot: Core microservice runtime for high-throughput telehealth orchestration
- Python / FastAPI: AI inference wrapper for symptom checker integration
- Apache Camel / Spring Integration: Translates data to HL7 FHIR (US) and EU national standards
- GCP GKE (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Isolated regional container orchestration
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: Region-locked primary data stores enforcing data residency
- GCP Cloud Pub/Sub: Asynchronous messaging buffer for prescription reliability

## Rationale
Region-isolated GKE clusters and databases guarantee strict GDPR and HIPAA data residency compliance. Asynchronous Pub/Sub messaging and local client caching ensure high availability and continuous operation during unstable rural internet connections.

Flutter Patient Mobile/Web App.analysis:
## Overview
Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. It enforces strict regional data residency and compliance with GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR.

## Key Elements
* Flutter Patient Mobile/Web App (Flutter container)
* Presentation Layer (Dart/Flutter UI component)
* State & Local Storage Manager (Hive / SQLite component)
* API Client & Region Router (Dio / HTTP component)
* WebRTC Video Module component
* Feature Flag & Configuration Provider component
* GCP API Gateway (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`)
* Consent & Profile Management Service

## Relationships
* Flutter App to GCP API Gateway via HTTPS (REST/GraphQL) and WSS (WebSockets) for signaling
* WebRTC Video Module to regional TURN/STUN relays for peer-to-peer media streams
* API Client & Region Router to GCP API Gateways (`europe-west3` or `us-central1`) based on user geolocation
* Feature Flag Provider to Consent & Profile Management Service via HTTPS for asynchronous sync

## Technology Stack
* Flutter: Cross-platform mobile and web client framework
* Hive / SQLite: Local client-side caching for offline resilience (<300 kbit/s)
* Dio / HTTP: Regional API routing and communication
* WebRTC: Low-bandwidth video consultations with regional TURN/STUN fallback
* GCP Cloud Build / GitHub Actions: Automated CI/CD deployment pipelines

## Rationale
This architecture ensures regional compliance and data residency by routing requests through localized GCP gateways. Client-side caching and WebRTC support reliable telehealth access for rural patients with unstable connections.

Clinician Portal.analysis:
## Overview
[The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. It ensures strict regional data residency, regulatory compliance, and high availability.]

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU/US) & Licensed Clinicians
- Flutter Patient Mobile/Web App
- Clinician Portal (React / Node.js)
- GCP API Gateway (Cloud Endpoints / Envoy)
- Core Telehealth Service (Go / Spring Boot)
- AI Inference Wrapper (Python / FastAPI)
- Pharmacy Integration Gateway (Apache Camel / Spring Integration)
- GCP GKE Regional Clusters (europe-west3, us-central1)
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL Databases

## Relationships
- Patient App to GCP API Gateway via HTTPS/WSS
- Clinician Portal to GCP API Gateway via HTTPS/WSS with JWT Authentication
- Session Controller to Core Telehealth Service via WSS (WebSocket Secure) for WebRTC signaling
- Prescription Dispatcher to Pharmacy Integration Gateway via gRPC / Protocol Buffers over TLS (mTLS via Envoy sidecar)
- Audit & Traceability Client to AI Inference Wrapper via HTTPS/REST

## Technology Stack
- GCP (europe-west3, us-central1): Target cloud infrastructure ensuring regional data isolation
- GKE & Kubernetes HPA: Container orchestration and autoscaling based on concurrent connections
- React & TypeScript: Frontend framework for low-latency UI rendering
- Node.js & Express: Backend component layer for session and prescription handling
- Go & Spring Boot: High-performance core backend services
- Python & FastAPI: AI inference wrapper for symptom checking
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: Regional relational data storage
- OpenTelemetry & GCP Cloud Logging: Distributed tracing and compliance log aggregation

## Rationale
[This architecture enforces GDPR and HIPAA compliance by isolating EU and US workloads into region-specific GKE clusters. Decoupled, stateless container design combined with gRPC, WSS, and Envoy proxies ensures low-latency communication, strict security, and resilience over unstable connections.]

GCP API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. The architecture uses regional GCP infrastructure to enforce strict data residency and compliance.

## Key Elements
* Patients and Licensed Clinicians (Users)
* GCP API Gateway (Cloud Endpoints / Envoy)
* Core Telehealth Service (Go / Spring Boot)
* Regional Identity Providers
* GCP GKE Regional Clusters (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`)
* Regional Health Authorities and Auditors

## Relationships
* Patients / Clinicians -> GCP API Gateway: Accesses telehealth services [HTTPS, WebRTC, OAuth2/JWT]
* GCP API Gateway -> Core Telehealth Service: Routes API requests [gRPC]
* GCP API Gateway -> Regional Identity Providers: Authenticates users [OIDC, HTTPS]
* Regional Health Authorities -> GCP API Gateway: Accesses audit endpoints [mTLS, signed JWTs, HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* GCP API Gateway / Envoy: Edge routing and local JWT validation to minimize latency
* gRPC over TLS: Inter-service communication for minimal serialization overhead on constrained networks
* OpenTelemetry / Cloud Trace: Distributed tracing across regional boundaries without data leakage
* Cloud Load Balancing: Anycast geo-routing to enforce physical entry-point segregation

## Rationale
Regional gateway deployments in `europe-west3` and `us-central1` enforce strict data residency requirements for GDPR and HIPAA compliance. Envoy-based traffic prioritization preserves availability for low-bandwidth users during active consultations.

Core Telehealth Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and AI-driven symptom checking for patients across the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance, and high availability over unstable connections.

## Key Elements
* Patients and Licensed Clinicians (Users)
* Flutter Patient Mobile/Web App and Clinician Portal (Containers)
* GCP API Gateway, Core Telehealth Service (Go/Gin), and AI Inference Wrapper (Python/FastAPI) (Containers)
* Consent & Profile Management Service and Pharmacy Integration Gateway (Containers)
* GCP GKE Regional Clusters (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`), Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, and GCP Cloud Pub/Sub (Infrastructure)

## Relationships
* GCP API Gateway -> Core Telehealth Service: Routes API requests [gRPC]
* Core Telehealth Service -> AI Inference Wrapper: Sends symptom-check requests with audit logging [gRPC]
* Core Telehealth Service -> Pharmacy Integration Gateway: Dispatches prescriptions asynchronously [GCP Pub/Sub]
* Core Telehealth Service -> Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: Persists session state and telemetry [TLS]

## Technology Stack
* Go / Gin: Selected for the Core Telehealth Service for high performance and low memory footprint.

GCP GKE Regional Clusters.analysis:
## Overview
A cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance, and high availability across distributed regional clusters.

## Key Elements
* **Patients & Licensed Clinicians**: End-users accessing mobile/web applications.
* **GCP GKE Regional Clusters**: Isolated container orchestration platforms deployed in `europe-west3` (EU) and `us-central1` (US).
* **Kubernetes Ingress Controllers (NGINX / Envoy)**: Manages TLS termination and ingress traffic routing.
* **Network Policy Enforcer (GKE Dataplane V2 / eBPF)**: Enforces pod isolation and namespace segmentation.
* **Log Forwarder & OTel Collectors (Fluentbit / OpenTelemetry)**: Streams audit logs and telemetry data.
* **Core Telehealth & AI Inference Services**: Microservices handling video streaming, prescriptions, and AI symptom analysis.

## Relationships
* **Patients/Clinicians to GCP API Gateway**: HTTPS/gRPC for application traffic.
* **Ingress Controllers to Internal Microservices**: HTTPS/gRPC for container-to-container communication.
* **Log Forwarder/OTel to GCP Cloud Logging/Monitoring**: gRPC/HTTPS for telemetry and audit streaming.
* **Network Policy Enforcer**: Layer 3/4 eBPF protocols for internal workload isolation.

## Technology Stack
* **GCP GKE Regional Clusters**: Container orchestration enforcing regional data boundaries.
* **GKE Dataplane V2 / eBPF**: Network policy enforcement for security isolation.
* **Fluentbit & OpenTelemetry**: Standardized logging and tracing for regulatory traceability.
* **ArgoCD**: GitOps continuous deployment ensuring consistent multi-region state.
* **Google Cloud KMS**: Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) for regional data-at-rest encryption.

## Rationale
This architecture isolates EU and US health data within designated GCP regions to satisfy strict GDPR and HIPAA compliance mandates. Multi-zonal cluster deployment and GitOps-driven zero-downtime upgrades guarantee continuous availability for critical telehealth consultations, even under unstable network conditions.

GCP Cloud Pub/Sub.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It guarantees regional data residency, strict regulatory compliance (GDPR/HIPAA), and high availability across unstable connections.

## Key Elements
- Patients (Mobile/Web App via Flutter)
- Licensed Clinicians (Clinician Portal via React / Node.js)
- GCP API Gateway (Cloud Endpoints / Envoy)
- Core Telehealth Service & Consent Service (Go / Spring Boot)
- AI Inference Wrapper (Python / FastAPI)
- Pharmacy Integration Gateway (Apache Camel / Spring Integration)
- GCP GKE Regional Clusters (europe-west3, us-central1)

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians access services via HTTPS/gRPC through GCP API Gateway.
- Core services publish e-prescriptions and audit logs to GCP Cloud Pub/Sub using gRPC/HTTPS with regional endpoint routing (`europe-west3-pubsub.googleapis.com`).
- Pharmacy Integration Gateway consumes e-prescription events via GCP Cloud Pub/Sub to deliver to national networks (EU) and US pharmacy systems.
- AI Inference Wrapper logs traceability data into regional GCP Cloud Pub/Sub audit topics.

## Technology Stack
- GCP Cloud Pub/Sub: Asynchronous messaging buffer with region-isolated topics for e-prescription reliability and audit logging.
- Avro / Protocol Buffers: Native schema validation at the Pub/Sub ingestion boundary to enforce data contracts.
- Terraform & GCP IAM: Infrastructure as Code and VPC Service Perimeters for security and regional data isolation.
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: Relational storage adhering to strict data residency rules per region.

## Rationale
This architecture uses GCP regional services and isolated Pub/Sub endpoints to strictly enforce EU and US data residency mandates. Asynchronous messaging via Pub/Sub ensures reliable prescription delivery for rural patients with unstable connections while maintaining complete audit traceability.
